_annotator: YOUR NAME -- fill in independently, don't look at the other file

_verdicts.needs_source: a number or factual claim with no specific source given
_verdicts.loaded_language: wording that pushes an opinion or emotion instead of describing neutrally
_verdicts.overgeneralization: absolute or sweeping wording (always, never, everyone ...)
_verdicts.vague_attribution: credits unnamed people (experts say, studies show ...) instead of a real source
_verdicts.ok: nothing the reader needs to double-check

_format: for each claim, set verdict to the one that fits best; note is optional

r01.sentence: The U.S. unemployment rate fell to 3.7% in 2023.
Wage growth was strongest among low-income workers, rising about 6% year over year.
Experts say the labor market remains tight.

r02.sentence: According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the unemployment rate averaged 3.6% in 2023.
In 2020 it peaked at 14.7% during the pandemic.

r03.sentence: Home prices have been skyrocketing in most major cities.
The median home price rose 40% between 2019 and 2023.

r04.sentence: Officials stressed that the situation at the border is not a crisis.
Crossings fell by roughly 30% in the first half of 2024, according to Customs and Border Protection.

r05.sentence: Studies show that remote workers are more productive.
One survey found that 68% of employees prefer working from home at least part of the time.

r06.sentence: The WHO estimates that immunization prevents 3.5 to 5 million deaths every year.

r07.sentence: Everyone knows that tax cuts always pay for themselves.
In reality, the Congressional Budget Office found that the 2017 tax law would add about $1.9 trillion to deficits over ten years.

r08.sentence: About 40% of Americans say they get news from social media regularly.

r09.sentence: The term "illegal alien" appears in older federal statutes, and some outlets still use it.

r10.sentence: Sales of electric vehicles doubled between 2021 and 2023.
Battery costs have fallen about 90% since 2010.
